title: Assembly
description: How a robot goes together. The robot record says what a mechanism IS; this says what somebody has to do to end up holding one. Note what is absent, and why: there is no build_time field (ADR-0011), because an assembly time nobody timed is the same invented number OpenBuildCore removed from print time (its ADR-0005). Torque specs are physical claims about fasteners and are citation-gated like joint limits. Steps form a DAG rather than a list, because 'do these in any order' and 'do this one first' are different facts and a numbered list cannot tell them apart.

robot_id.description: The robot this assembly builds. Stored, not resolved — same rule as a part_id (ADR-0006). A validator run over both files checks that every link_id named in a step exists in that robot.

steps.description: A directed acyclic graph, expressed by each step naming what it depends on. A cycle is a validation error. A step with no depends_on may be done first; two steps with the same dependencies may be done in either order, and saying so is information a numbered list destroys.

measured_build_time.description: Only ever a figure somebody timed. Absent means build time cannot be estimated and the answer is that it requires building one — the same shape as OpenBuildCore's measured_throughput and refused for the same reason (ADR-0011). A sum of per-step guesses is not a measurement, it is a guess with more decimal places.

how_measured.description: Who built it, how many times, whether the parts were already printed and sorted, and whether this was their first attempt. A first build and a fifth build are different numbers and the difference is large.

builder_experience.description: The author of an assembly is the fastest possible builder and the least representative one.

action.description: What a person does, in a sentence. Prose for a human; nothing computes against it.

depends_on.description: step_ids that must be complete first. Absent or empty means this step has no predecessor — a genuine claim that it can be done first, not an omission.

joins.description: link_ids from the robot record that this step brings together. This is the field that ties an assembly to a mechanism rather than leaving it as a standalone document.

tools.description: What the step needs in hand, as lowercase tokens: hex-2.5, torque-driver, loctite-243, press. A tool nobody owns is a blocker discovered at the bench, which is exactly the kind OpenBuildCore exists to move earlier.

irreversible.description: True for a step that cannot be undone without destroying a part — a press fit, a cut, a permanent adhesive, a heat-set insert. Declaring it is what lets a build guide warn BEFORE rather than after, and it is a fact about the step that no downstream tool can infer.

verify.description: How the builder confirms the step actually worked, before the next step buries it. A step whose failure is only discoverable three steps later is the expensive kind.

fastener.description: Exactly one of part_id or spec. A fastener from OpenPartsCore's mechanical namespace is preferred, because then its facts have a home with citations; spec is the escape hatch for a size nobody has catalogued yet.

part_id.description: An OpenPartsCore mechanical entry. Stored, not resolved (ADR-0006).

spec.description: e.g. 'M3x8 SHCS', 'M3 heat-set insert OD 4.6'. Prose, because a fastener nobody catalogued has no id to point at. A validator may warn that this should become a part_id.

torque_nm.description: A torque spec is a physical claim about hardware and is gated on a citation exactly like a joint limit. ABSENT MEANS UNKNOWN, never 'hand tight' and never 'snug' — the failure mode is a stripped insert in a printed part, which is unrecoverable and common. Most hobby assemblies will have null here, and that is a true statement about the available evidence rather than a gap to fill with a number from feel.

threadlock.description: Whether the joint is specified to receive a threadlocking compound. A fastener in a mechanism that vibrates and has neither threadlock nor a locking feature is a fastener that will back out; recording its absence is more useful than leaving it unsaid.
